ei.title: The World of Sports Taking Responsibility
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Stewardship of the environment has become an issue that affects almost all aspects of our lives. Consequently, individuals and organizations constantly strive to make small changes to their daily habits to build a greener environment. Individuals practice a more mindful approach to their way of living to reduce their environmental impact while organizations strive to modify their way of doing business to minimize their effect on the environment. The world of sports is no exception and it has a lot of potential to be part of the solution. Many sporting events have a negative impact on the environment because they require massive structures to host them. To draw more spectators, sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting bigger, consuming larger areas of land and requiring greater amounts of building materials for construction. Whenever a hectare of grassland is cleared for a construction site, there is a loss of nature. Every ton of concrete and steel used in the building foundation and structure is produced, transported, poured, and put together by equipment and facilities that emit waste into the ground and atmosphere. Then, after the stadium is completed, large amounts of water, electricity, and other forms of resources are consumed to operate and maintain the facility. Every sporting event affects the environment before, during, and even after it. For example, a long-track speed skating competition can only take place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. As long as the competition is on, the track needs to be kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems while the temperature, humidity, and air quality inside the stadium also have to be maintained for optimal ice conditions. Additionally, all of the stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to travel to and from the stadium, often from other cities or even from abroad. In fact, more than 25% of the emissions generated by the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics are estimated to be caused by fan travel and accommodations. During the event, spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they consumed leave trash cans overflowing. After the event has ended, in addition to the significant amount of trash that needs to be disposed of, the effects those people caused and the emissions generated from their travel continue to have a lasting negative impact on air quality. Alarm bells sounded when research suggested the possibility that nearly one in every four English soccer stadiums could be partially or completely flooded in the near future due to climate change and extreme weather events. Some research even predicted that by 2050 almost half of the cities that once hosted the Winter Olympics would not be able to do so again for lack of snow and ice. Also, the US Open Tennis Championships organizers implemented an “extreme heat policy,” having mandatory short breaks for players to cool down during matches, after a few quit their matches due to extreme heat. As more sports are affected by climate change, concerns are growing. There is light at the end of the tunnel, however. The sports community is optimistic that it can reduce its environmental impact by taking two main steps: transitioning to more sustainable operations before, during, and after events and raising awareness among the public about their impact. Efforts to adopt more responsible approaches have been made by various organizations, and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is leading the way by setting a good example. The IOC set up the Sport and Environment Commission decades ago and declared the environment as essential to the Olympic Movement, in addition to sports and culture. It has since encouraged host nations to adopt more environmental approaches to putting on the Olympics. As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000 Sydney Summer Olympics became the world’s largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Olympics adopted a new energy recycling system which used the curling hall’s air conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms in the venue. Also, for the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics, the Olympic speed-skating venue was built with salvaged timber. The Olympic Park for the 2012 London Summer Olympics, which was built on industrial land that was once contaminated, was converted to the biggest urban park in Europe. Then at the 2020 Tokyo Summer Olympics, electricity was generated with hydrogen instead of fossil fuel, which supplied power for many residential buildings in the Olympic Village and Paralympic Village. Thanks to its popularity, sports is a powerful tool for universally raising awareness about environmental responsibility. Simply put, the sports industry influences billions of individuals that are involved in sports either as spectators, athletes, or organizers. Through sports, strategies to increase awareness and educate the public about the importance of sustaining the environment have shown good results. Research has found that fans are receptive to ecological or environmental initiatives organized at sporting events, and many are willing to change their lifestyle habits accordingly. The social status of athletes can have a strong effect, too. For example, high-profile athletes and coaches can be sports ambassadors to foster environmental consciousness among fans, especially young people who look up to them. The broad appeal of sports becomes a vehicle to reach many people at once. While sports provide us with such immense benefits, we ─ along with sporting event organizers ─need to be aware of the adverse environmental effects that sports have at times. As long as we are all aware of the effects, we can take steps toward finding ways to minimize or even completely eliminate them. While Green Sports Day, on October 6th, is a global event that promotes environmentally friendly sports, maybe it’s time we declare every day a day to encourage greater sustainability in sports. World Link Bioremediation A Sustainable Solution to Ocean Pollution On April 20, 2010, an enormous explosion shook the Deepwater Horizon drilling platform in the Gulf of Mexico, causing a significant oil leak into the sea. Over a three-month period, approximately 134 million gallons of oil, comparable to more than 200 Olympic swimming pools, flowed into the sea before it was eventually halted. Despite continuing restoration efforts, the sea has not yet fully recovered. One approach to addressing the issue of oil contamination is bioremediation, a restoration method that utilizes bacteria. Some types of bacteria naturally exist in marine environments and possess the capability to break down various components of oil. When an oil spill occurs, these bacteria are attracted to the oil and begin to multiply. As they grow, they release enzymes that break down oil into carbon dioxide and water. Although this process may take several weeks or months, it represents a more sustainable method of cleaning up oil spills compared to conventional approaches involving harmful chemicals. Bacteria can also play a role in the process of plastic decomposition. When plastic enters the ocean, some bacteria are attracted to it, leading to their growth and reproduction. Similar to the process of breaking down oil, the bacteria release enzymes that break down plastic into smaller molecules, ultimately resulting in carbon dioxide and water. It’s not all good news, however. There are challenges associated with bioremediation. The breakdown of oil or plastic by bacteria, as mentioned earlier, can be a time-consuming process requiring weeks or months. These bacteria can also be sensitive to specific environmental conditions such as temperature and sea water constituents. Despite these challenges, there is no doubt that bioremediation holds promise as a technology for oil spill or plastic cleanup in the ocean. Because the bacteria used in this process occur naturally, they do not need to be transported to the polluted site. Bioremediation may be a more effective way to confront contamination problems and reduce environmental harm.

questions.passage: Many sporting events have a negative impact on the environment because they require massive structures to host them.  To draw more spectators, sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting bigger, consuming larger areas of land and ①<u>requiring</u> greater amounts of building materials for construction.  Whenever a hectare of grassland is cleared for a construction site, there is a loss of nature.  Every ton of concrete and steel ②<u>used</u> in the building foundation and structure ③<u>are produced</u>, transported, poured, and put together by equipment and facilities that emit waste into the ground and atmosphere.  Then, after the stadium is completed, large amounts of water, electricity, and other forms of resources ④<u>are consumed</u> to operate and maintain the facility.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① requiring: getting bigger, consuming ~ and requiring ~ — 앞의 consuming과 and로 이어지는 분사구문(V-ing)이라 적절
② used: concrete and steel used in the building — 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사(쓰인)로 수동 관계라 적절
③ are produced → is produced: 주어가 'Every ton of concrete and steel(콘크리트와 강철 1톤마다)'인데 진짜 주어의 핵심은 단수 'Every ton'이다. 뒤의 concrete and steel에 낚여 복수 are를 쓰면 안 되고 단수 is가 맞다 ←정답
④ are consumed: large amounts of water, electricity, and other forms of resources are consumed — 주어 amounts(복수)에 맞는 복수 수동태라 적절
det.tip: Every + 단수명사가 주어면 동사도 단수. Every ton ... is produced.

questions.passage: For example, a long-track speed skating competition can only take place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval track ①<u>is frozen</u> until it is 3 to 5 cm thick.  As long as the competition is on, the track needs ②<u>to keep</u> frozen by specialized refrigeration systems while the temperature, humidity, and air quality inside the stadium also have ③<u>to be maintained</u> for optimal ice conditions.  Additionally, all of the stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to travel to and from the stadium, often from other cities or even from abroad.  In fact, more than 25% of the emissions generated by the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics ④<u>are estimated</u> to be caused by fan travel and accommodations.  During the event, spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they consumed leave trash cans overflowing.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① is frozen: the ice ~ is frozen — 얼음은 '얼려지는' 대상이므로 수동태(be + p.p.)가 적절
② to keep → to be kept: the track needs to be kept frozen에서 트랙은 '계속 얼려지는' 대상이라 수동의 to be kept가 맞다. 능동의 to keep(누군가를 얼리다)은 부적절 ←정답
③ to be maintained: the temperature, humidity, and air quality ~ have to be maintained — 온도·습도 등은 '유지되는' 대상이라 수동태가 적절
④ are estimated: more than 25% of the emissions ~ are estimated — 주어가 복수(emissions)라 복수 동사가 적절
det.tip: 트랙이 '얼려지는' 것이므로 수동. need + to be + p.p. = ~되어야 한다.

questions.passage: It has since encouraged host nations to adopt more environmental approaches to putting on the Olympics.  As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000 Sydney Summer Olympics ①<u>became</u> the world’s largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Olympics adopted a new energy recycling system ②<u>which used</u> the curling hall’s air conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms in the venue. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① became: the Olympic Village ~ became the world's largest solar-powered suburb — 주어 Village에 맞는 과거 정동사라 적절
② which used: a new energy recycling system which used ~ — 앞의 system을 받는 주격 관계대명사 + 과거동사라 적절
③ was converted: The Olympic Park ~ was converted to the biggest urban park — 삽입절(which was built ~) 뒤에 오는 문장의 본동사(수동태)라 적절
④ which supplying → which supplied: '~, which supplied power(그런데 그것이 전력을 공급했다)'는 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법의 관계대명사절이다. 관계사절에는 시제를 갖춘 정동사가 필요하므로 supplied가 맞고, 동사 없는 supplying은 틀리다 ←정답
det.tip: 콤마 + which는 관계대명사절. 그 안에는 -ing가 아니라 정동사가 와야 함.

questions.passage: The sports community is optimistic that it can reduce its environmental impact ①<u>by taking</u> two main steps: transitioning to more sustainable operations before, during, and after events and raising awareness among the public about their impact.  Efforts to adopt more responsible approaches ②<u>have been made</u> by various organizations, and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is leading the way by setting a good example.  The IOC set up the Sport and Environment Commission decades ago and ③<u>declaring</u> the environment as essential to the Olympic Movement, in addition to sports and culture.  It has since encouraged ④<u>host nations to adopt</u> more environmental approaches to putting on the Olympics.  As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000 Sydney Summer Olympics became the world’s largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Olympics adopted a new energy recycling system which used the curling hall’s air conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms in the venue.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① by taking: reduce its impact by taking two main steps — 전치사 by 뒤 동명사(V-ing)라 적절
② have been made: Efforts ~ have been made by various organizations — 주어 Efforts(복수)에 맞는 복수 수동태라 적절
③ declaring → declared: The IOC set up ~ and declared the environment as essential에서 앞의 과거동사 set up과 and로 이어지는 병렬 구조다. 같은 과거 정동사 declared가 맞고, 분사형 declaring은 병렬을 깨뜨려 틀리다 ←정답
④ host nations to adopt: encouraged host nations to adopt more environmental approaches — 'encourage + 목적어 + to부정사(~가 …하도록 장려하다)' 구조라 적절
det.tip: A and B 병렬은 형태를 맞춤. set up과 짝이면 declared(둘 다 과거동사).

questions.passage: Thanks to its popularity, sports is a ①<u>weak</u> tool for universally raising awareness about environmental responsibility.  Simply put, the sports industry influences billions of individuals that are involved in sports either as spectators, athletes, or organizers.  Through sports, strategies to ②<u>increase</u> awareness and educate the public about the importance of sustaining the environment have shown good results.  Research has found that fans are ③<u>receptive</u> to ecological or environmental initiatives organized at sporting events, and many are ④<u>willing</u> to change their lifestyle habits accordingly.  The social status of athletes can have a strong effect, too.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: weak(→powerful): 스포츠는 인식을 높이는 강력한 수단이다
det.analysis:
① weak(약한) → powerful(강력한): 앞에서 스포츠는 인기 덕분에(Thanks to its popularity) 환경 인식을 높이는 도구라 했으므로, 뒤이어 수십억 명에게 영향을 준다는 흐름상 '강력한(powerful)' 수단이 맞다. weak는 정반대라 부적절 ←정답
② increase(높이다): strategies to increase awareness — 인식을 '높이는' 전략이라는 문맥에 적절
③ receptive(수용적인): fans are receptive to ecological initiatives — 팬들이 환경 활동을 '기꺼이 받아들인다'는 문맥에 적절
④ willing(기꺼이 ~하는): many are willing to change their lifestyle habits — 습관을 '기꺼이' 바꾸려 한다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: powerful(강력한) ↔ weak(약한). 스포츠의 popularity가 근거.

questions.passage: One approach to addressing the issue of oil contamination is bioremediation, a restoration method that utilizes bacteria.  Some types of bacteria ①<u>naturally</u> exist in marine environments and possess the capability to break down various components of oil.  When an oil spill occurs, these bacteria are attracted to the oil and begin to ②<u>disappear</u>.  As they grow, they release enzymes that break down oil into carbon dioxide and water.  Although this process may take several weeks or months, it represents a more ③<u>sustainable method</u> of cleaning up oil spills compared to ④<u>conventional</u> approaches involving harmful chemicals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① naturally(자연적으로): Some types of bacteria naturally exist in marine environments — 박테리아가 바다에 '자연적으로' 존재한다는 문맥에 적절
② disappear(사라지다) → multiply(증식하다): 기름 유출이 생기면 박테리아가 기름에 이끌려 오고, 바로 뒤에서 'As they grow(그들이 자라면서)'라고 하므로 수가 '늘어나는' multiply가 맞다. disappear는 정반대라 부적절 ←정답
③ sustainable method(지속 가능한 방법): a more sustainable method of cleaning up oil spills — 유해 화학물질을 쓰는 기존 방법보다 '더 지속 가능한' 방법이라는 문맥에 적절
④ conventional(기존의): conventional approaches involving harmful chemicals — 화학물질을 쓰는 '기존' 방식이라는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: multiply(증식하다) ↔ disappear(사라지다). 뒤의 As they grow가 근거.

det.korean: 스포츠계가 환경 영향을 줄이려고 밟는 것.
det.analysis:
① a strict penalty(엄격한 처벌): 처벌을 준다는 내용이 아니라 부적절
② several excuses(여러 변명): 변명을 한다는 흐름이 아니라 부적절
③ one final warning(마지막 경고 하나): 경고가 아니라 실천 방법을 말하므로 부적절
④ two main steps(두 가지 주요 단계): 빈칸 뒤 콜론(:) 다음에 '지속 가능한 운영으로 전환하기'와 '대중의 인식 높이기' 두 가지를 나열하므로 '두 가지 주요 단계'가 맞다 ←정답
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤 콜론(:) + transitioning ~ and raising ~ 두 항목 나열 → two main steps.

det.korean: 박테리아가 자연적으로 존재하기 때문에 필요 없는 것.
det.analysis:
① paid for in advance(미리 값이 치러지는): 비용을 낸다는 내용이 아니라 부적절
② frozen before use(사용 전 얼려지는): 얼린다는 언급이 없어 부적절
③ transported to the polluted site(오염된 장소로 옮겨지는): 빈칸 앞에서 '이 박테리아는 자연적으로 존재하기 때문에(occur naturally)'라고 했으므로, 이미 그곳에 있어 '오염된 장소로 옮길' 필요가 없다는 흐름이 맞다 ←정답
④ replaced every day(매일 교체되는): 교체와 무관해 부적절
det.tip: occur naturally(자연적으로 존재) → 옮길(transport) 필요 없음.

questions.passage: One approach to addressing the issue of oil contamination is bioremediation, a restoration method that utilizes bacteria.  Some types of bacteria naturally exist in marine environments and possess the capability to break down various components of oil.  When an oil spill occurs, these bacteria are attracted to the oil and begin to multiply.  As they grow, they release enzymes that break down oil into carbon dioxide and water.  Although this process may take several weeks or months, it represents a more sustainable method of cleaning up oil spills compared to conventional approaches involving harmful chemicals.  Bacteria can also play a role in the process of plastic decomposition.  When plastic enters the ocean, some bacteria are attracted to it, leading to their growth and reproduction.  Similar to the process of breaking down oil, the bacteria release enzymes that break down plastic into smaller molecules, ultimately resulting in carbon dioxide and water.

questions.passage: Stewardship of the environment has become an issue that affects almost all aspects of our lives.  Consequently, individuals and organizations constantly strive to make small changes to their daily habits to build a greener environment.  Individuals practice a more mindful approach to their way of living to reduce their environmental impact while organizations strive to modify their way of doing business to minimize their effect on the environment.  The world of sports is no exception and it has a lot of potential to be part of the solution.  Many sporting events have a negative impact on the environment because they require massive structures to host them.  To draw more spectators, sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting bigger, consuming larger areas of land and requiring greater amounts of building materials for construction.  Whenever a hectare of grassland is cleared for a construction site, there is a loss of nature.  Every ton of concrete and steel used in the building foundation and structure is produced, transported, poured, and put together by equipment and facilities that emit waste into the ground and atmosphere.  Then, after the stadium is completed, large amounts of water, electricity, and other forms of resources are consumed to operate and maintain the facility.  Every sporting event affects the environment before, during, and even after it.  For example, a long-track speed skating competition can only take place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick.  As long as the competition is on, the track needs to be kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems while the temperature, humidity, and air quality inside the stadium also have to be maintained for optimal ice conditions.  Additionally, all of the stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to travel to and from the stadium, often from other cities or even from abroad.  In fact, more than 25% of the emissions generated by the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics are estimated to be caused by fan travel and accommodations.  During the event, spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they consumed leave trash cans overflowing.  After the event has ended, in addition to the significant amount of trash that needs to be disposed of, the effects those people caused and the emissions generated from their travel continue to have a lasting negative impact on air quality.  Alarm bells sounded when research suggested the possibility that nearly one in every four English soccer stadiums could be partially or completely flooded in the near future due to climate change and extreme weather events.  Some research even predicted that by 2050 almost half of the cities that once hosted the Winter Olympics would not be able to do so again for lack of snow and ice.  Also, the US Open Tennis Championships organizers implemented an “extreme heat policy,” having mandatory short breaks for players to cool down during matches, after a few quit their matches due to extreme heat.  As more sports are affected by climate change, concerns are growing.  There is light at the end of the tunnel, however.  The sports community is optimistic that it can reduce its environmental impact by taking two main steps: transitioning to more sustainable operations before, during, and after events and raising awareness among the public about their impact.  Efforts to adopt more responsible approaches have been made by various organizations, and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is leading the way by setting a good example.  The IOC set up the Sport and Environment Commission decades ago and declared the environment as essential to the Olympic Movement, in addition to sports and culture.  It has since encouraged host nations to adopt more environmental approaches to putting on the Olympics.  As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000 Sydney Summer Olympics became the world’s largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Olympics adopted a new energy recycling system which used the curling hall’s air conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms in the venue.  Also, for the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics, the Olympic speed-skating venue was built with salvaged timber.  The Olympic Park for the 2012 London Summer Olympics, which was built on industrial land that was once contaminated, was converted to the biggest urban park in Europe.  Then at the 2020 Tokyo Summer Olympics, electricity was generated with hydrogen instead of fossil fuel, which supplied power for many residential buildings in the Olympic Village and Paralympic Village.  Thanks to its popularity, sports is a powerful tool for universally raising awareness about environmental responsibility.  Simply put, the sports industry influences billions of individuals that are involved in sports either as spectators, athletes, or organizers.  Through sports, strategies to increase awareness and educate the public about the importance of sustaining the environment have shown good results.  Research has found that fans are receptive to ecological or environmental initiatives organized at sporting events, and many are willing to change their lifestyle habits accordingly.  The social status of athletes can have a strong effect, too.  For example, high-profile athletes and coaches can be sports ambassadors to foster environmental consciousness among fans, especially young people who look up to them.  The broad appeal of sports becomes a vehicle to reach many people at once.  While sports provide us with such immense benefits, we ─ along with sporting event organizers ─need to be aware of the adverse environmental effects that sports have at times.  As long as we are all aware of the effects, we can take steps toward finding ways to minimize or even completely eliminate them.  While Green Sports Day, on October 6th, is a global event that promotes environmentally friendly sports, maybe it’s time we declare every day a day to encourage greater sustainability in sports.

위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]에 따라 영작하시오.

[조건]
(1) a, athletes, can, effect, have, of, social, status, strong, The를 모두 사용할 것

(3) 영어로 쓸 것

det.analysis:

- '강한 영향을 미칠 수 있다'는 'can have a strong effect(강한 효과를 가질 수 있다)'로 표현한다
det.tip: A of B = B의 A. The social status of athletes(운동선수의 사회적 지위).
